transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. I, um... I came in today because I keep getting these awful, unwanted thoughts. I just constantly feel like I’ve missed something critical. 

It could be a wrong number in a data release at work, or an unlocked back door, or even just a bill paid from the wrong account. And... even when I know I checked it, my mind just won't let go of the possibility that I’ve caused some kind of disaster. It's just very overwhelming.
When these thoughts occur, do you feel compelled to perform specific actions or repeat certain mental steps, like double-checking things or counting, to try to relieve the distress?

Yes, I do. To try and calm myself down, I end up... well, reopening spreadsheets, or rereading my emails line by line. With the other things, I'll check the locks and the payment confirmations over and over again. 

I have to do it in a very specific, set order until it finally feels 'safe' to me. It just takes up so much time. Some nights I’m still sitting at my desk hours later, just checking, and I haven't actually finished anything.

latest_inference.note: The patient's description of intrusive, distressing thoughts (obsessions) followed by repetitive, ritualized checking behaviors performed to alleviate anxiety (compulsions) is highly characteristic of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder. The specificity of the rituals and the time-consuming nature of these behaviors strongly point to F42.2, effectively ruling out generalized anxiety (F41.1) and social phobia (F40.1).
